tiles.h3: Combined Sewers Fill in a Storm

blocks.intro: All of Evanston is served by combined sewers, so storm water and household wastewater share the same pipes.

items.body: Only during heavy rain points to a full city sewer. On a dry day, your lateral is blocked.
The city maintains the main. The pipe from your home is yours.
A backflow valve or [overhead sewer system](/evanston/overhead-sewer-systems) keeps sewer water out.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.body: The timing tells you a lot. If sewage came up during or right after a heavy storm, the combined sewer in the street likely filled and pushed water back. If it came up on a dry day, the problem is almost always in your lateral: roots, grease or a break. The fix is different. A blocked lateral needs cleaning or repair. Storm backups need a backflow valve or an overhead sewer. Our camera tells us which one you're dealing with.

blocks.h2: Sewer Backup Questions From Evanston Homeowners

items.q: Why does my basement back up only in big storms?
items.answer: Evanston's sewers carry rain and wastewater together. In heavy storms, they fill and push water back into the lowest drains.

items.q: Do you clean up after a sewage backup?
items.preview: We fix the plumbing. A restoration company cleans up.
items.answer: We clear the line and repair the cause. For cleanup and drying, call a water restoration company. Many Evanston homeowners call both.

items.q: Is a sewer backup covered by insurance?
items.answer: Many policies need a sewer backup rider. Check with your agent.

items.preview: An overhead sewer for repeat backups.
items.answer: For repeat backups, an overhead sewer. For lighter risk, a backflow valve or standpipe.

items.q: How much does sewer backup service cost in Evanston?
items.preview: It depends on the cause. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what caused it and how we reach the line. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
